pages.title: sqx: Query CSV, JSON, logs and websites with SQL from the command line
pages.description: sqx is a free, single-binary CLI that runs SQL on CSV, TSV, JSON, JSON Lines and text piped from Unix streams, and adds SQL functions to fetch URLs, parse HTML, look up DNS and match regex.

mainEntity.name: How do I query a CSV file with SQL from the command line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pipe the file into sqx and query the table named stdin: cat users.csv | sqx "SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM stdin GROUP BY country". sqx detects the format, cleans up column names and infers numeric types automatically.

mainEntity.name: Can I join a CSV file with a JSON file using SQL?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Load each file as a named table with -f and join them in one query: sqx -f users=users.csv -f events=events.jsonl "SELECT ... FROM users JOIN events ON events.user_id = users.id".

mainEntity.name: Does sqx need SQLite or a database server installed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. sqx is one self-contained binary with SQLite built in. There is no runtime, server, driver or shared library to install on macOS, Linux, Windows or FreeBSD.

mainEntity.name: Can sqx fetch web pages and extract HTML with SQL?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Functions such as http_status(url), html_title(url), html_meta(url, 'description') and html_links(url) fetch pages through a persistent on-disk cache, so each URL is downloaded only once.

mainEntity.name: Is sqx free and open source?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. sqx is free software released under the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later.
